intro.title: Establish your company in Portugal with the right legal foundations

blocks.text: Are you planning to start a business in Portugal, either on your own or with business partners?

Setting up a company involves more than completing registration formalities. Choosing the appropriate legal structure, defining shareholder relationships and preparing the company's constitutional documents are important decisions that can influence its future development.
**As a lawyer registered with the Paris and Lisbon Bar Associations, I assist international entrepreneurs and investors with the legal aspects of establishing companies in Portugal.**
I provide personalised legal advice in English and French, from the initial structuring of your project through to the company's incorporation.
**Discuss Your Company Formation Project**
The appropriate legal structure depends on your project, the number of shareholders, your business objectives and the way you intend to organise your company.
The main corporate structures in Portugal include:
Unipessoal Lda | Single-Member Private Limited Liability Company
A *Sociedade Unipessoal por Quotas* is a private limited liability company with a single shareholder.
It is commonly used by entrepreneurs who wish to establish a company on their own, with a legal personality separate from that of the shareholder.
Lda | Private Limited Liability Company
A *Sociedade por Quotas* is a private limited liability company generally formed by two or more shareholders.
It is a common structure for business projects involving several partners and offers flexibility in organising the company's management and shareholder relationships.
SA | Public Limited Liability Company
A *Sociedade Anónima* is a corporate structure generally suited to projects of a certain scale, particularly those requiring a more complex shareholding or governance structure.
**My company formation practice primarily focuses on Lda and Unipessoal Lda structures.**
I help you assess the legal implications of the available options and identify the structure most appropriate for your project.

sections.title: Legal Support Throughout the Incorporation Process

blocks.text: I assist with the main legal steps involved in establishing your company in Portugal.
1. Structuring Your Project
Before incorporation, we review the essential characteristics of your proposed business:

items: The intended business activities.
The number and identity of shareholders.
The proposed ownership and management structure.
The company's share capital.
The registered office and other relevant organisational matters.

blocks.text: This initial review helps identify the legal decisions that should be addressed before registration.
2. Preparing the Company's Legal Documents
I assist with drafting and reviewing the company's articles of association, taking into account its proposed activities and ownership structure.
Where appropriate, I can also advise on arrangements between shareholders, including the preparation of a separate shareholders' agreement.
3. Incorporation and Commercial Registration
I assist with the necessary legal formalities, which may include:

items: Checking or obtaining the company name, where required.
Preparing incorporation documents.
Coordinating the execution of the relevant documents.
Registering the company with the Portuguese Commercial Registry.
Assisting with beneficial ownership registration (*Registo Central do Beneficiário Efetivo*, or RCBE).

blocks.text: The applicable steps and documentation depend on the company's structure and the circumstances of its shareholders.

sections.title: Beyond Incorporation: Legal Support as Your Company Develops

blocks.text: Company formation is only the beginning of a business's legal life.
As your company grows, you may need assistance with commercial contracts, shareholder arrangements, corporate governance, changes in share capital or other legal matters.
I also advise existing Portuguese companies on specific transactions and ongoing corporate legal needs.
**Explore Corporate Legal Services in Portugal**
Can a foreign national establish a company in Portugal?
Yes. Foreign nationals can generally establish or participate in Portuguese companies without being Portuguese residents, subject to the applicable legal and administrative requirements.
Can I establish a Portuguese company remotely?

In many cases, incorporation can be organised without all shareholders travelling to Portugal. The available procedures depend on the circumstances, the required documents and the applicable execution formalities.
What is the difference between a Unipessoal Lda and an Lda?
A Unipessoal Lda has a single shareholder, while an ordinary Lda generally has two or more shareholders. Both are private limited liability company structures, although certain legal rules differ.
Do I need a shareholders' agreement when creating a company?

A shareholders' agreement is not generally mandatory. However, it may be particularly useful when several shareholders are involved, as it can establish arrangements concerning decision-making, transfers of quotas and other aspects of their relationship.
Does incorporating a company automatically allow me to reside in Portugal?
No. Company incorporation and immigration status are separate legal matters. Establishing or owning a Portuguese company does not, by itself, grant a right of residence.
If your project also involves relocating to Portugal, the applicable immigration requirements should be assessed separately.

I work with entrepreneurs and company directors who need a trusted legal adviser familiar with their business and available to assist as legal questions arise.

Depending on your needs, we can arrange assistance for a particular matter or discuss a more regular working relationship.
**Let's Discuss Your Company's Needs**
Does a Portuguese Lda need a shareholders' agreement?

A shareholders' agreement is not generally mandatory. However, it can be particularly useful when a company has several shareholders, as it allows them to define arrangements concerning governance, transfers of quotas, decision-making and other aspects of their relationship.
What is the difference between articles of association and a shareholders' agreement?
The articles of association are the company's constitutional document and are subject to applicable registration and publicity requirements.
A shareholders' agreement is a separate contractual arrangement between its parties. It can address matters that the shareholders wish to regulate between themselves, subject to applicable law.
Can a new shareholder join an existing Portuguese company?

Yes. Depending on the circumstances, this may involve a transfer of quotas, a share capital increase or another legally appropriate transaction. The required documentation and formalities depend on the company's structure and the proposed arrangement.
Does my company need a lawyer on an ongoing basis?
Portuguese companies are not generally required to retain a lawyer for their day-to-day operations.
However, regular legal support can be valuable for companies managing contracts, shareholder relationships, corporate changes or other legal matters.

intro.title: Legal assistance for buying or selling property in Portugal

blocks.text: Buying or selling property in Portugal involves important legal and financial commitments.

Whether you are purchasing a home, investing in Portuguese real estate or selling a property, having independent legal advice can help you understand the transaction, identify potential risks and protect your interests.
**As a lawyer registered with the Paris and Lisbon Bar Associations, I assist international buyers, sellers and investors with real estate transactions in Portugal.**
I provide personalised legal support in English and French, from the initial review of the property documentation through to the completion of the transaction.
**Discuss Your Real Estate Project**
Legal support throughout your purchase
Purchasing a property involves several stages, each requiring careful legal consideration.
I assist buyers with the following steps.
1. Legal Due Diligence
Before committing to a purchase, it is essential to verify the property's legal and administrative situation.
Depending on the circumstances, my review may include:

items: Ownership and registration details.
Land Registry documentation (*certidão permanente*).
Tax registration and property information (*caderneta predial*).
Relevant planning and licensing documentation.
Existing mortgages, charges or other registered encumbrances.
Condominium documentation and outstanding charges, where applicable.
Other legal issues relevant to the proposed acquisition.

blocks.text: The objective is to identify potential risks before you enter into binding contractual commitments.
2. Promissory Purchase and Sale Agreement (CPCV)
The *Contrato-Promessa de Compra e Venda* (CPCV) is an important stage of many Portuguese real estate transactions.
I assist with drafting, reviewing and negotiating the agreement, paying particular attention to:

items: The identification of the property and the parties.
The purchase price and deposit (*sinal*).
The conditions and deadlines for completion.
Contractual obligations and remedies in the event of non-performance.
Protective clauses relating to bank financing, where appropriate.
Other conditions specific to your transaction.

blocks.text: I also advise on the applicable requirements concerning the execution and authentication of signatures.
3. Bank Financing and Purchase Formalities
If you are financing your purchase through a Portuguese bank, I can assist with the legal aspects of the financing process and coordinate relevant steps with the bank or mortgage intermediary.
I also assist with the preparation and issuance of the payment documents (*guias de pagamento*) for the applicable acquisition taxes, including:

items: Property Transfer Tax (*Imposto Municipal sobre as Transmissões Onerosas de Imóveis*, or IMT).
Stamp Duty (*Imposto do Selo*, or IS).

blocks.text: The taxes and any applicable exemptions depend on the circumstances of the transaction and the buyer.
4. Completion of the Purchase (Escritura)
I assist with preparing for and attending the final signing of the transaction, whether through a notarial deed or another legally accepted form of completion.
My assistance may include:

items: Reviewing the final transaction documentation.
Coordinating with the notary, solicitor or other competent professional.
Checking the legal conditions for completion.
Attending the signing and providing explanations or interpretation where required.
Assisting with the relevant post-completion registration formalities.

blocks.text: Legal assistance to prepare and complete your sale
Selling a property also requires careful preparation, particularly when the owner lives abroad or cannot attend the transaction in person.
I assist sellers with:

items: Reviewing the property's legal documentation.
Identifying legal or administrative issues that should be addressed before the sale.
Reviewing and negotiating the CPCV.
Advising on contractual obligations and completion deadlines.
Coordinating the legal documentation required for the final deed.
Assisting with completion and, where appropriate, representation by power of attorney.

blocks.text: My role is to help you anticipate potential difficulties and complete the transaction with greater legal certainty.
**You do not necessarily need to travel to Portugal for every stage of your real estate transaction.**
I regularly assist international clients who live outside Portugal or are unable to attend certain formalities in person.
Depending on the circumstances, I can coordinate documentation, communicate with the relevant parties and represent clients through an appropriate power of attorney.
The possibility of remote execution or representation depends on the legal requirements and practical arrangements applicable to each transaction.
Do I need a lawyer to buy property in Portugal?
A lawyer is not legally required to purchase property in Portugal.
However, independent legal advice is strongly recommended to review the property's documentation, assess contractual risks and protect your interests throughout the transaction.
What is a CPCV in Portugal?
A CPCV (*Contrato-Promessa de Compra e Venda*) is a promissory purchase and sale agreement through which the parties undertake to complete a property transaction under agreed conditions.
It commonly provides for a deposit, completion deadlines and consequences if either party fails to fulfil its contractual obligations.
Should legal due diligence be completed before signing the CPCV?
Ideally, the relevant legal checks should be carried out before signing the CPCV or making binding commitments.
This allows potential issues to be identified and addressed before the buyer assumes contractual obligations.
Can I buy property in Portugal without travelling there?
In many cases, yes. Certain stages of the transaction may be organised remotely, and representation through a power of attorney may be possible.
The appropriate arrangements depend on the transaction, the documentation and the formal requirements involved.
What taxes apply when buying property in Portugal?
Property acquisitions in Portugal generally involve IMT and Stamp Duty.
The amounts payable depend on factors such as the property's value, nature and intended use, as well as any exemptions or special rules applicable to the buyer.

intro.title: Legal assistance with your relocation and residence in Portugal

blocks.text: Moving to Portugal, obtaining a residence permit or applying for Portuguese citizenship involves legal and administrative procedures that vary depending on your nationality and personal circumstances.
Whether you are planning to relocate, already living in Portugal or seeking to formalise your residence status, understanding the applicable requirements is essential.
**As a lawyer registered with the Paris and Lisbon Bar Associations, I assist international clients with immigration, residency and nationality matters in Portugal.**
I provide personalised legal advice in English and French to help you understand the procedures, prepare the required documentation and navigate the relevant administrative formalities.
**Discuss Your Immigration or Residency Matter**

sections.title: Visas and Residence Permits for Non-EU Nationals

blocks.text: If you are a national of a country outside the European Union, your relocation to Portugal may require an appropriate visa or residence permit.
The applicable procedure depends on your circumstances and the purpose of your stay.
I assist clients with matters relating to:

items: Residence visas for employment or self-employment.
Residence procedures for entrepreneurs and business owners.
Residence visas based on qualifying passive income.
Residence procedures for remote workers.
Family reunification.
Residence permit applications and renewals.
Other immigration procedures depending on individual circumstances.

blocks.text: My assistance may include assessing the relevant legal requirements, reviewing supporting documentation, preparing applications and advising on interactions with the competent authorities.
The available procedures, eligibility conditions and processing times depend on the applicable legislation and administrative circumstances.

sections.title: Residence in Portugal for EU Citizens and Their Families

blocks.text: Citizens of the European Union benefit from specific rights of entry and residence in Portugal under EU and Portuguese law.
However, certain registration formalities apply depending on the duration and circumstances of their stay.
I assist EU citizens and eligible family members with:

items: Registration certificates for EU citizens (*Certificado de Registo de Cidadão da União Europeia*, or CRUE).
Residence documentation for eligible non-EU family members.
Questions relating to the exercise of EU residence rights in Portugal.
Applications for documentation evidencing permanent residence rights.

blocks.text: Permanent Residence
EU citizens who have legally resided in Portugal for a continuous period of five years may acquire a right of permanent residence, subject to the applicable legal conditions.
The relevant certificate serves to document that right.
Different documentary procedures may apply to non-EU family members.
I assist clients in assessing their eligibility and preparing the appropriate applications.
Portuguese nationality may be available through different legal routes, depending on the applicant's circumstances.
I assist with nationality matters involving:

items: Acquisition of Portuguese nationality based on legal residence.
Nationality through marriage or a legally recognised de facto union with a Portuguese national.
Nationality by descent or family connections.
Other nationality procedures where applicable.

blocks.text: My assistance includes assessing the relevant eligibility conditions, identifying the necessary documents and supporting the preparation and submission of applications.
**Nationality requirements depend on the legal basis of the application and the legislation in force at the relevant time.**

sections.title: Tax Identification Numbers and Fiscal Representation

blocks.text: Obtaining a Portuguese tax identification number (*Número de Identificação Fiscal*, or NIF) is often an important administrative step for individuals with personal, financial or professional interests in Portugal.
Depending on your circumstances, a NIF may be needed for activities such as opening a bank account, acquiring property or establishing a company.
I assist international clients with:

items: Applications for Portuguese tax identification numbers.
Fiscal representation arrangements where required or appropriate.
Related administrative formalities.

blocks.text: The obligations applicable to non-residents depend on their circumstances and the rules in force.

sections.title: Legal Support for Your Projects in Portugal

blocks.text: Relocating to Portugal may also involve buying a property or establishing a business.
Alongside immigration and residence matters, I provide legal assistance with:

items: **Real estate transactions:** legal due diligence, promissory purchase and sale agreements, and completion of property acquisitions.
**Company formation:** establishing and structuring Portuguese companies.
**Corporate legal services:** supporting companies with their legal needs as they operate and develop.

blocks.text: This approach allows you to obtain coordinated legal advice on different aspects of your project in Portugal.
**Explore My Legal Services**
Do EU citizens need a visa to live in Portugal?
No. EU citizens do not need a visa to enter or reside in Portugal under the applicable EU free movement rules.
However, those staying for more than three months are generally required to complete the relevant residence registration formalities, subject to the applicable conditions.
Does creating a Portuguese company automatically grant a right of residence?
No. Incorporating or owning a Portuguese company does not automatically grant a residence permit.
The appropriate immigration route must be assessed separately.
Can I apply for Portuguese citizenship after living in Portugal?
Portuguese nationality may be available following a qualifying period of legal residence, provided the applicant meets the applicable statutory conditions.
The required period and other eligibility criteria must be assessed under the legislation applicable to the application.
Can I apply for Portuguese citizenship through marriage?
Portuguese law provides a route to nationality through marriage or a legally recognised de facto union with a Portuguese national, subject to the applicable legal requirements.
Is a Portuguese NIF required before moving to Portugal?
A NIF may be necessary for certain transactions and administrative procedures, even before you become a Portuguese resident.
Whether you need one immediately depends on the steps you intend to take.

Whether you are planning to move to Portugal, need assistance with your residence status or wish to explore your eligibility for Portuguese citizenship, I can help you identify the relevant legal procedures.
